prior_exposed_data: NRF-07 newly trained checkpoint MSE and 8/16 original suffix leakage at their respective training depths
design: Paired suffix-depth intervention on each of six final NRF-07 CPU weights, with exactly the same halfway state h_(train_depth/2), same projection bases, same ridge-trained heads and heldout task MSE in each suffix comparison.
fixed_representation: Train model depth T. Use h_(T/2) on fold 1/5/6 and fit one set of decoder bases and ridge heads for that checkpoint, unchanged between suffix comparisons.
outcomes: random control median of complete objective J at lambda=1
supervised minus random median J at lambda=1 for both suffix lengths
entire first-crossover lambda (when finite and meaningful)
primary_directional_gate: At least 5 of 6 frozen checkpoints show greater supervised local Jacobian leakage when suffix expands from 8 to 16. Report all six including failures.
secondary: For each model evaluate whether supervised-minus-random median J changes sign from suffix length 8 to length 16; report both trained-depth cohorts and every lambda-grid entry even when primary gate fails.
random_aggregation: Median of eight complete (MSE+lambda*leakage^2) objectives. Never use separate median MSE or median leakage.
strict_replay: Check regenerated checkpoint SHA-256 against the frozen NRF-07 summary, and compare original-length metrics to NRF-07 summary at tight numeric tolerance. If mismatch, stop and report, preserving all received state.
claim_boundary: Within a pre-trained model and fixed shadow states this is a suffix-only intervention. It does not equal a full-depth retraining comparison or prove that every longer recurrence has greater leakage. All models, folds, controls and lambda selection were exposed in earlier studies, so conclusions remain exploratory.
